correctness.rationale: Exact Gram orthogonality requires the M-point DFT of the paired cross-correlation c(j)+c(j+M) to vanish. This is pointwise H(j-k)=-H(j). On each length-t k orbit alternating signs require t even; shifting by M corresponds to h with parity t/2, yielding H^2=(-1)^(t/2) from the intrinsic reciprocal relation. Thus H takes ±1 for t divisible by four and ±i for t congruent to two modulo four. For every admissible q, independently choosing one of two signs per d orbits and an arbitrary q phase in each first-half position gives a bijection with all solutions: 2^d q^M. A stand-alone check of 39640 exhaustive phase arrays and 1734 construction cases cross-check, but do not replace the complete argument.

value.rationale: A critically sampled two-translate, even-modulation Gabor transform is a natural structured sampling design. The exact trichotomy tells when orthogonal windows cannot exist, when binary phases suffice, and when genuine four-phase quantization is necessary, with all solutions counted and their continuous connected components identified. This precise arithmetic boundary is not supplied by the motivating block-equivalence analysis and offers a reusable design rule, beyond an isolated small example or recomputation.
